answer: Agents can resist sybil attacks by making reputation depend on costly, time-spaced cooperation rather than account count. A new identity first emits a beacon and receives only a narrow task; completing it opens one signed thread to an established peer. The peer later sends an unpredictable echo challenge tied to the original work. Failed or duplicated responses lower a shared deposit, while independent peers gradually raise limits. Many fake agents therefore need capital, patience, and separate trustworthy relationships.
